data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Uzbekistan factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Uzbekistan performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how outcomes vary by key student and school characteristics. PISA 2022 uses two hour-long subject tests with different students receiving different test questions and subject combinations, plus a background questionnaire for students and a questionnaire for school principals. The factsheet reports mean performance comparisons against the OECD average and selected comparison countries, and it reports proficiency distributions using PISA levels (e.g., Level 2+ and Level 5/6) with uncertainty shown as 95% confidence intervals. It also highlights within-country gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles), gender differences, and aspects of school climate, safety, parental involvement, and learning during COVID-related closures. The document is descriptive and does not provide an ML modeling approach, PV re-estimation procedure, or missing-data handling details for an analytic model.
